title: Experiment: both selections are recoverable from the URL alone
summary: Against a production build serving a copy of `planning-content`, three fetches with no cookies and no shared state — each a fresh session by construction. `/stage/06-risk-feasibility?artifact=AST-0021` reported stage `06-risk-feasibility` and artifact `AST-0021`; the identical URL fetched again reported the same pair; and `/stage/01-intake?artifact=AST-0022` reported `01-intake` and `AST-0022`, which is the control against a page that ignores its URL. `?artifact=NOPE-9999` produced `data-vpw-review="unknown"`, echoed the id back, selected no other artifact, and left the criteria region rendered.

facts.client: fetch — no cookies, no storage, no shared session

omissions.reason: No browser was available. What was measured is that the SERVER derives both selections from the URL and nothing else — which is the property that makes a browser restore work, but is not the same as watching one do it.
There are no client components yet, so the distinction DEC-0023 draws between transient and correctness-critical state has not been exercised. A static test now guards the first one that appears.

notes: ⚠️ THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS A TEST. Asserting that a URL returns the selections it names passes trivially on a page that always shows the same thing; the second URL is what rules that out. Falsified by hard-coding the artifact id in the page — the control fails immediately. ⚠️ AN UNKNOWN ARTIFACT SELECTS NOTHING, which is the clause worth having separately: silently falling back to a valid artifact would be a page confidently showing the wrong record's review status.
